title: Canary ladder + golden-answer diff for weight-only INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) profile integration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an integration and regression validation harness for weight-only INT8 profiles (GPTQ and AWQ) that pairs a progressive canary ladder with a golden-answer diff technique. This ticket covers CI hooks, deterministic prompt sets, shadow/compare runs against FP16 baseline, automated metric computation (KLD/top-k divergence, answer parity, semantic-similarity via embeddings), and rollback triggers for accuracy drift. Goal: safe, automated rollouts of new quant profiles with measurable, explainable deltas and clear rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic golden-answer corpus (>= 250 prompts) committed to repo and integrated into nightly run
CI job that runs weight-only INT8 GPTQ and AWQ conversions, executes inference against FP16 baseline, and produces a diff report published to artifacts
Canary ladder orchestration: shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% with automated checks at each step
Automated metric thresholds configured: answer-parity >= 95% OR embedding-similarity cosine >= 0.93 and top-k KLD < 0.12; failing runs block rollout
Dashboard charting token-level logprob delta, answer mismatch rate, and top-k KLD for each model/profile variant
Rollback policy and runbook documented and tested using a simulated degraded profile in staging
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike and design doc drafted. Chosen golden-answer approach after spike comparing BLEU vs embedding-similarity on 100 calibration prompts.

2026-02-20: Deterministic prompt set expanded to 300 prompts covering short answers, multi-turn, QA, code, and summarization. Seeded and committed to repo at //git.company.com/r/quant-profiles/golden-corpus
2026-02-27: Conversion CI job prototype (gptq + awq) added to ci/quant-profiles with containerized converter and per-run artifact capture. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8123

2026-03-03: Telemetry schema agreed: metrics.name {answer_mismatch_rate, embedding_cosine_median, topk_kld_95p, token_logprob_delta_p50}, and instrumentation added to runtime telemetry bridge (PR 8175).
2026-03-08: Canary ladder orchestration sketched; opted for progressive percentages (shadow, 0.5%, 2%, 10%) for low-latency paths. Draft runbook uploaded to Confluence.

2026-03-10: First staging run completed against A100 and heterogeneous node with mixed precision: observed embedding_cosine_median=0.946, answer_mismatch_rate=3.8% on GPTQ profile — within thresholds. Next: formalize chaos tests.
decisions: Use a dual metric (answer parity + embedding similarity) rather than BLEU/ROUGE alone to capture semantic equivalence across paraphrases.
Run both GPTQ and AWQ conversion paths in CI for parity and select per-model preferred profile automatically via metric ranking.
Canary ladder percentages chosen to minimize customer exposure while accelerating signal: shadow, 0.5%, 2%, 10% (then 50/100%).
Define a conservative fail-block: answer_mismatch_rate > 8% OR embedding_cosine_median < 0.90 OR topk_kld_95p > 0.18 triggers immediate rollback.
tradeoffs: Gold corpus size vs run time: 300 prompts gives stable metrics within 30m on A100 but slows CI; will run a smaller fast-suite on PRs and full-suite nightly.
Embedding-similarity thresholds can mask subtle hallucination modes; combined with token-logprob deltas to catch confidence shifts.
Running both GPTQ and AWQ doubles CPU conversion time in CI; accepted longer CI in exchange for automated parity checks and reduced manual validation overhead.

test_plan: Unit: converter unit tests covering weight-only conversions for GPTQ/AWQ with synthetic tensors
Integration: CI job runs conversion -> inference vs FP16 baseline -> produce diff artifact and metrics
Nightly: full golden-answer diff run across hardware matrix [A100, H100, T4] with report stored for drift detection
Chaos: inject a failing profile in staging to validate rollback automation and alerting
A/B: small-traffic canary to validate real-world signal and latency regressions
rollout_plan: Shadow mode: convert and route copies to shadow cluster, no customer traffic. Validate metrics for 48h.
Canary step 1: 0.5% traffic for 4h, automated checks run every 30m. If pass, advance.
Canary step 2: 2% traffic for 6h, automated checks run every 30m. If pass, advance.
Canary step 3: 10% traffic for 12h, include latency SLO checks. If pass, escalate to 50% then 100% per deployment window.
Rollback: immediate rollback and alert to oncall if fail-block criteria met; incident checklist and postmortem required.
telemetry_queries: metrics.query: SELECT PERCENTILE(embedding_cosine,50) FROM quant_diff WHERE model=$MODEL AND profile=$PROFILE AND window=1h
logs.query: search for answer_mismatch events AND request_id IN last_1h to sample side-by-side outputs
kld.distribution: compute topk KLD per request and publish 95th percentile per-profile
delta.logprob: bucket token logprob delta p50/p90 and alert on shifts > 0.6 median
notes: Next steps: wire the canary ladder into runtime routing layer and finalize the PR that surfaces per-request sample diffs in the CI artifact. Schedule a cross-team review with Support and SRE the week of 2026-03-15. Keep FP8 comparison out of scope for rollout but collect FP8 conversion outputs during shadow runs for later analysis.
